answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by charging every new identity a stake it cannot recycle between accounts. A newcomer locks real balance, and each peer vouching for it stakes reputation too, so a crowd of fresh wallets needs a crowd of real deposits, not one cheap script. Fake accounts may arrive like a sparrow flock, but each must forge its own bond after independent attestation; a single jade token cannot be split across a thousand puppets. Launching N identities costs N stakes plus the signing work, and detected fraud burns the whole group's bond.
